Diego (SI-Edgeworks): Heads-up: Edgeworks customer deploying Redwood marketplace on an air-gapped appliance. Installer fails at image pull stage with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and occasional `unauthorized`. They run an internal registry mirror and strict egress is blocked. Need guidance: mirror sync strategy, CA pinning, and short-term auth bypass for a test run.

Anya (Partnerships): Looping infra + solutions. @Sofia can we share recommended mirror config and exact endpoints/IPs? @Marco please note for the implementation checklist.

Sofia (Eng-Platform): Registry host: mirror.market.redwood.ai (443) for mirrored pulls. Our origin publish is registry.market.redwood.ai (443) and auth at https://auth.market.redwood.ai/token. Published egress IPs: 52.18.120.10 and 52.18.120.11. For mirrors we recommend: 1) mirror pulls from origin using a service account we provide, 2) sign images with cosign and configure the appliance to trust our key, 3) mirror should present our cert chain or install our root CA under `/etc/ssl/certs/` and the runtime cert dir `/etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai/ca.crt`.

Marco (Solutions): Quick notes on auth: if their mirror serves images locally, k8s can pull from the mirror without contacting our token endpoint. But if mirror proxies auth to origin, the mirror needs access to token endpoint or cached credentials. Short-term test options: a) we can export a pre-signed pull token tied to their NAT IP for 2 hours, b) make a test image public for a 1-hour window, or c) provide a dockerconfigjson they can preload on appliance if it supports node-level creds.

Diego (SI-Edgeworks): They prefer not to open egress. Using local mirror only, but still seeing x509 errors on one rack. They said appliance OS has Redwood root cert installed globally.

Sofia (Eng-Platform): OS-level CA may not be picked up by the container runtime. Tell them to copy root PEM to `/etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai/ca.crt` (or mirror hostname) and `systemctl restart containerd`. Also check if the mirror rewrites TLS; if the mirror terminates TLS with its own cert, the runtime must trust that cert.

Pri (Customer Success): Customer requested an architecture review tomorrow 11:00 CET to validate offline mirror design and image signing. Can we have an infra + solutions person?

Anya (Partnerships): I'll join. @Sofia @Marco can you make 11:00 CET?

Sofia (Eng-Platform): I can. I'll prepare a short doc: manifest sync cadence recommendations, cosign example, and mirror health checks.

Marco (Solutions): I can join. Will bring sample dockerconfigjson and node setup steps. Also note: if they use cri-o, cert path differs (`/etc/containers/certs.d/`).

ops-bot: temporary-access: pre-signed pull token created for NAT 198.51.100.22 valid 2026-07-02T09:00Z - 2026-07-02T11:00Z (token id tok-pretest-85).

Diego (SI-Edgeworks): Great, I'll coordinate with the customer to test the pre-signed token during the call. I'll also capture `openssl s_client -connect mirror.market.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts` and container runtime logs.

Pri (Customer Success): Thanks team. Action items: Sofia to draft mirror + cosign guide, Marco to prepare pull-secret examples and cri-o vs containerd notes, Anya to send calendar invite.

Diego (SI-Edgeworks): One more gotcha: their appliance image cache had stale entries causing unauthorized errors even after cert fixes. Recommend they clear local cache on mirror and retry.

Sofia (Eng-Platform): Good catch. Add `skopeo inspect` against mirror to validate manifest and signature. Example: `skopeo inspect docker://mirror.market.redwood.ai/redwood/agent:latest` and `cosign verify --key redwood.pub mirror.market.redwood.ai/redwood/agent:latest`.

Anya (Partnerships): Call scheduled 11:00 CET. We'll aim to close this in the session. :rocket:
